key_insight: A context-aware Markov decision model can tailor Type 2 diabetes follow-up timing to patient risk, rather than using the same fixed visit interval for everyone.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help primary care teams schedule visits more efficiently by matching follow-up frequency to current labs, recent hospitalizations, and underlying risk context.
method: Used EHR data from 22,154 patients with Type 2 diabetes across 10 primary care clinics.
Built patient contexts with PCA on health trajectories plus clustering with patient-level features.
Learned follow-up interval policies with a Contextual Markov Decision Process and compared them with fixed-interval benchmarks.
evidence_signal: In evaluation, the CMDP policy lowered expected cumulative cost versus an ADA-like fixed follow-up policy, with about 34.8% reduction in the higher-comorbidity context and 6.4% in the lower-comorbidity context.
watch_item: The model was derived from retrospective EHR data, so prospective validation is needed before routine implementation.
paper_title: Context-Aware Optimization of Follow-Up Intervals for Type 2 Diabetes Care Using Markov Decision Processes
